title: Control-Table-Driven Pipelines and Asset Discovery
summary: Drive Fabric pipelines from a Warehouse control table instead of hard-coded activities, and keep the item IDs it needs fresh with an automated, API-based inventory of every workspace and item.
audience: Data platform engineers, Fabric administrators, orchestration and DevOps owners

pages.title: Overview
pages.description: What the control-table framework and asset inventory solve, when to use them, what you build, and how the pages fit together.

pages.title: Asset discovery and inventory
pages.description: Choose the right API, authenticate safely, build the inventory notebook and tables, and use the catalog for governance, orchestration, cost, security and CI/CD.

pages.title: Framework design and decisions
pages.description: Principles, end-to-end flow, prerequisites, topology, a decision table against alternatives, and design guidance for ordering, retries, concurrency and restarts.

pages.title: Warehouse objects and seed data
pages.description: Convert T-SQL scripts to stored procedures, create the control table, run log, procedures and views in a Fabric Warehouse, and seed the first tasks.

pages.title: Notebook dispatcher (GUID launcher)
pages.description: Run notebooks by item ID so renames cannot break orchestration: options compared, the dispatcher notebook, polling, identity and capacity behavior.

pages.title: Build the master pipeline
pages.description: Guard step, stage lookups, ForEach settings, the per-task body with logging, Switch on task type, failure paths and a reusable notification pipeline.

pages.title: Extended scenario and workshop
pages.description: Scale the plan from five to twenty tasks, populate the control table, inspect the lookups and run timelines, and rebuild the pipeline as a hands-on workshop.

pages.title: Operations, security and checklist
pages.description: Health-check queries, monitoring, troubleshooting, security, CI/CD with variable libraries, observability, and a go-live checklist with references.
